name: Approval without vote
title: RECOMMENDATION FOR SECOND READING on the Council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council laying down Union procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human use and establishing rules governing the European Medicines Agency, amending Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007 and Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 and repealing Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, Regulation (EC) No 141/2000 and Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006
part_text:
The European Parliament has approved the Council's position on a new law setting out how medicines for human use are authorised and supervised across the European Union, and how the European Medicines Agency works. The law replaces several older rules on medicines, including rules on rare-disease and children's medicines. Parliament and the Council had already reached an agreement, so Parliament accepted the text without changes.

- **What changes:** One set of EU rules replaces several older regulations on approving and monitoring medicines.
- **Who it affects:** Patients, medicine makers, national health authorities and the European Medicines Agency.
- **What happens next:** Parliament's President and the Council's President sign the law, and it is published in the Official Journal.
